english: This area is rife with Dragon's corruption. Hunt down any corrupt wolves or shards of corruption you find. The grawl to the east are also extremely dangerous.
This area of the Beacon of Ages is under repair due to the Kryptis attack.
This area...ripe for ambush. Do you sense it, too? No, of course not. But we will not be fooled. Search for traps!
This arena's been here as long as the Legions have been in this region. Think for a second about all the blood soaked into this ground. Makes me giddy.
This armor could be placed on a snowman.
This armor fits me like a glove.
This atlas documents common plants and animals native to Kryta and is full of rich, colorful illustrations and sketches.
This barrel holds metal scraps, bars, and jotun swords.
This basket appears to be used for holding valuable goods.
This battle is over!
This bed reeks! And dusting once a century doesn't count as housekeeping, you know.
This bench, while of Elonian design, is quite ordinary.
This blight's got me seeing red! Purge it! Purge them all!
This book by Scholar Alainn goes into meticulous detail about the various species of plants found in Kryta.
This book by Watchman Pramas is the definitive tome on the history of the ancient relic used in the war against the charr.
This book catalogs human royal and noble families throughout the history of Tyria, and their involvement in the politics of their era.
This book chronicles the most famous warriors in Tyria.
This book covers a wide variety of creation myths that have been proposed by cultures and religions throughout the history of Tyria.
This book describes governmental organizations from traditional monarchies to more obscure forms of rulership.
This book discusses the theory that one can bind a ghostly spirit to a material object. It is unable to prove that this is possible.
This book is not as old as the relics that surround it. Many of the pages have been torn out, and the title reads, "Logs of the Orrian Expedition by Mollen, Esteemed Explorer."
This book is well-worn and contains almost illegible notes in the margins. Someone wedged a folded piece of paper between the pages.
This book maps in great detail the geographical landscape of the Shiverpeaks.
This book mocks the fruitless efforts of alchemists to turn lead into gold, listing many asuran researchers who have wasted their careers pursuing the myth that it's possible.
This book, by Ogden Stonehealer, describes the events of 1078 AE that caused the Transformation of the Dwarves.
This bookshelf holds an eclectic collection of items, everything from treatises on ancient Krytan lore to asuran theories on sylvari metabolism. The tomes are fastidiously arranged in order.
This boss can only be damaged by those who have Blue Resonance.
This boss can only be damaged by those who have Green Resonance.
This boss can only be damaged by those who have Red Resonance.
This boss is invulnerable to all attacks from the mortal realm.
This can't be their main force. Everyone, stay ready for another surge!
This cannon exhausts heated gas due to heavy use.
This cart contains a variety of books, most of which are new or show signs of wear from repeated browsing. However, one dusty tome sits forgotten in the corner: "Honoring the Ancestor Tree."
This cart offers a variety of books, including "Constellations: Legends Told in Stars," "The Mystery of the Bloodstones," and "Beyond the Mists."
This cart specializes in books on ancient heroes. On display are copies of "Torn Between Two Gods: The Story of Mhenlo," "Eve of Destruction," and "Firebrand: Tales of Cynn."
This cat meows expectantly. You sense that it's an emissary of charitable entities.
This catalog of desert plants is dry and academic. It describes healing properties associated with each plant, but gives no evidence to support its conclusions.
This chest looks like it contains some personal belongings, but nothing of particular value.
This chest radiates heat. It doesn't seem to open through any normal means.
This clanmarshal ruled your former home?
This close to Jormag, the grawl are at risk. It is in their nature to revere power. We must divert their attention.
This collection of notes is entitled, "The Secrets of Necromancy."
This collective consciousness (along with some asura, humans, and stubborn norn) put the Great Destroyer to rest.
This construct is gonna be fun!
This copy of "The Shining Blade Manual," written by Master Exemplar Bartholos in 1089 A.E., is a first edition. Updated versions of it have been handed out to recruits ever since.
This could be the perfect place to uncover Vabbi's recent history.
This creature has the ability to mark characters for death, causing them to die if they're unable to remove the curse in time.
This creature is drawn to the scent of ley magic.
This creature is unstable and will explode on death.
This curious device looks like nothing you've seen before, but it appears to have some role in food preparation, judging from the inside being spattered with some kind of pungent sauce.
This desert's really something.
This detailed account of the final fight with the Elder Dragon Zhaitan includes a list of all Pact members who were killed. The feats of %str1% are called out as having been critical to the victory.
This device is very finicky, and the eggheads in research and development didn't send very good instructions. We need to grab that ley energy and get out of here before the Inquest shows up.
This djinn is exhausted. Use the jackal's Pounce skill to give him a shield and protect him.
This door leads into the Astral Ward's Beacon Command Center.
This driftwood would be a nice place to sit down and relax, if it weren't for all the crabs around.
This drink looks undrinkable.
This egg needs to stay warm. Bring it to Johanna before it gets too cold.
This empty pen shows that I am weak. A trained pet will show my power.
This enchanted armor will help us defend Tarir from the Mordrem.
This ends here!
This entire village will feed Mordremoth!
This explains why the people here worship him so fanatically.

This far from Trinity, it's vital that the Pact support lines remain clear. Our mission is to move forces south and reinforce the coming strike on Arah. Leagues of hostile territory lie before us, but we'll show the Risen what a little determination and a lot of firepower can do as we carve our way clear to their capital.
This fishing rod is made of a sturdy wood, but it is missing its line and lure. It appears Mai was a capable fisherwoman, as the handle is worn from use.
This flier is torn and weathered, featuring a drawing of a crazed quaggan rolling in a large pile of dead fish to the delight of a boisterous crowd. Below are the words "Kookoochoo the Inane."
This flier is torn and weathered, featuring a drawing of a quaggan engulfed in flames while an audience looks on and cheers. Below are the words "Kookoochoo the Infernal."
This flier is torn and weathered, featuring a drawing of a quaggan foaming at the mouth and attacking his one-time followers. Below are the words "Kookoochoo the Insane".
This flier is torn and weathered, featuring a drawing of a quaggan standing before a robed magistrate as three of his former followers testify. Below are the words "Kookoochoo the Indicted".
This flier is torn and weathered, featuring a drawing of a quaggan with a wispy, pathetic puff of smoke issuing from its mouth. Below are the words "Kookoochoo the Incombustible."
This flier is torn and weathered, featuring a drawing of a quaggan with iron chains about his wrists and ankles being escorted away by Lionguard. Below are the words "Kookoochoo the Incriminated".
This flier is torn and weathered, featuring a drawing of quaggan and his followers persecuting those defending an asura with bandaged fingers. Below are the words "Kookoochoo the Intolerant".
This flier is torn and weathered, featuring a drawing of quaggan that's puffed up and enraged upon a stage as fearful passersby look on. Below are the words "Kookoochoo the Infuriated."
This flyer is torn and weathered, featuring a drawing of a quaggan being beaten by angry pirates yet still bearing a strange grin. Below are the words "Kookoochoo the Incautious."
This flyer is torn and weathered, featuring a drawing of a quaggan seemingly spewing vitriol to a shocked audience. Below are the words "Kookoochoo the Invidious."
This flyer is torn and weathered, featuring a drawing of a quaggan standing proudly above a dozen broken and defeated foes, below the words "Koocoochoo the Indomitable."
This foe will only take damage from those with a negative magnetic signature.
This foe will only take damage from those with a positive magnetic signature.
This formation is used in service of a vastly superior ally. Like me, for example.
This gate is shut. The last time the gates were open, our king was killed by outsiders. Now we mourn our king, now we name a new king, now the gates must be closed.
This generator is currently active and producing Aetherblade holograms. Destroy it to stop the holograms from generating.
This goes over here—careful with that—and there we go. Another portal spike.
This golem could help us explore the ruins, but it's missing parts. If you find any, bring them to me.
This golem is a relic from an ancient time. Despite the passage of centuries, it looks to be in remarkable condition.
This grid covers the entire city, so no one needs to worry about a chak bursting through the ground—assuming there are no power fluctuations in the perimeter defenses.
This hammer, wielded by King Jalis Ironhammer, was the magical catalyst. It caused the success of the Rite of the Great Dwarf.
This has been fun, but I think I'll be teleporting to safety now. Ha!
This headstone stands in memory of Kilroy Stoneskin, who defeated Gulnar Irontoe in battle. A master brawler, his deeds will not be forgotten. Another line of runes is below.
This history book is a scholarly look at how the Searing forever changed the landscape of Ascalon. It compares maps of the region from before and after the catastrophe.
This hole looks fit for a crab.
This instructional volume arms the reader with tips for public speaking, in particular those readers looking to enter a life of public service.
This is Battleground Plaza, where up-and-coming golemancers have their their mechanical creations duke it out. Golem VS. Golem! Krewes fight day and night to prove they're the superior golemancers.
This is Marjory Del... Mm.
This is Marjory and Kasmeer... No.
This is Taimi! I'm not available to talk right now. Y'know, busy inventing novel technologies that change how we communicate.
This is a fascinating location. The chak are drawn to the ley energy. Which is likely why it's been abandoned.
This is a fine day to be outdoors. Is there any way I can help you in your travels?
This is a fool's errand, Eir.
This is a good spot. Don't forget, our work will be heard throughout the forest. Prepare yourselves.
This is a good—ah!—a good start, but I can still carry more!
This is a job for me. Stay here, I've got this.
This is a temporary staging ground for warbands arriving to the Citadel, before they're assigned bunks. In an emergency, it's also here for displaced gladia.
This is a test of the Rata Novus Emergency Alert system. When you hear this tone—(tone)—listen carefully for instructions.
This is all that remains of Nahtem, youngest of the three high ritual priests of Elona entrusted by Turai Ossa with a Vision Crystal shard.
This is an unauthorized balcony extension.
This is as good as any spot. I can't wait to see the look on those plants when the chak show up.
This is between me and the commander. You can die next.
This is crazy talk. I should go back to bed.
This is dangerous country to roam alone.
This is for every person that fell in Shaemoor, in Ascalon Settlement, in Nebo Terrace. This is for us! Forward the Seraph!
This is going a bit rougher than expected, isn't it?
This is going well.
This is gonna hurt!

This is home to the Exalted, souls bound to armor who live in Tarir, the Forgotten City, which lies within a grand cenote constructed of gold. There, the Exalted await something they call Glint's legacy. And beyond the walls, their outposts stand watch, defending the city from the ever-advancing Mordrem.
This is hopeless. These Nuhoch are as bad as the Itzel. They don't listen!
This is it, boys and girls. We move on the centaur camps today.
This is looking good. I should be able to make repairs now. Bring me any extras, if you have them.
This is natural selection at work.
This is no natural storm! Brogun must have found something to the east!
This is none of my business.
This is not like our own spawning grounds. But on the plus side, it is very wet.
This is not my home. I came from the east, hoping to bring this place back into balance after the arrival of Zinn. One day I hope it will be at peace and I can return home.
This is not the time for bug hunting.
This is old. Hundreds of years old.
This is our island! Get them off our shore!
This is our land!
This is personal. You're not invited.
This is pointless. Come on, Ikniu. We'll have to find another way to convince your leaders.
This is purely for science, and not because I skipped breakfast.
This is so COOL!
This is so generous, thank you.
This is so infuriating. These people work hard enough without a bunch of thieving, yellow-bellied, underhanded, foul-smelling, worthless, rotten pirates wrecking everything.
This is the big one.
This is the final console. It has some damage, but looks salvageable. Keep me safe!
This is the last entry. Return the book to the table.
This is the last nearby rally point. Mordrem have destroyed the rest!
This is the place to do it.
This is their home. We're the guests, they're the hosts. They should start showing some hospitality.
This is unacceptable! We need more cores!
This is very familiar! We're almost there.
This is what I have to do. I think Romke would understand my choice.
This is what we're fighting to protect. Please: help save my people, and my best scouts will be at your disposal.
This is where the Dream called me, where I am needed most. I didn't choose to come here, I simply came. Protecting this place is my Wyld Hunt.
This is where the Seraph, Wyld Hunt, and Peacemakers are gathering soldiers to fight the Sinister Triad.
This is, or was, a famous human site known as Serenity Temple. I'm considered an expert on it. Are you at all curious about it?
This isn't fair.
This isn't good. The Forged are taking more of an interest in the Order.
This isn't our land. We didn't let it get in this shape. Why should we be expected to work it?
This isn't what I signed on for when I became a bodyguard.
This journal contains notes about a sea beast's skeleton. There are sketches of what the creature looked like when alive, including a humorous scene in which it's eating Inquest agents.
This journal describes the tragic story of a human mage caught up in his obsession to summon a djinn, believing it would grant him phenomenal cosmic power.
This journey will likely be frought with danger, but the greater danger would be not destroying those spectral weapons. Their deactivation could be the key to our maintaining our hold on the temple.
This jungle is dying.
This jungle is weak.
This little chick has fallen from its nest. You might be able to get it back up there, though!
This message shows coordinates for their communications tower. Gives us a leg up. Follow me.
This mining operation isn't cheap, you know! Research notes allow us to perform valuable research and development for new products and modifications.
This mission must be completed. Take a SHORT break, then get back out there.
This mural of the forgotten god Abaddon is weathered with age and marred by water damage, but his eyes seem to glitter with icy cunning, and his countenance is still suffocatingly imposing.
This must be Kormir. Hail to you, "Goddess of Truth." We need your help.
This must be a lair!
This must be so hard on you. I'm sorry.
This must be the five hundredth dolyak I've escorted in my time. Not easy work.
This object is being weakened. Additional Mining Laser attacks will make it susceptible to damage.
This object takes 10%% less damage from enemy attacks and cannot be upgraded further.
This old hammer resembles the weapons built in Turai Ossa's era, but everyone knows that Turia Ossa wielded an iconic sword and shield.
This old plank seems to have washed up during high tide and became lodged here. Perhaps someone would know more about it.
This one fights well.
This one is difficult.
This one's on you! I was gathering lentils.
This one's overwhelming me!

This pack of gathering tools offers all the benefits of the Piñata gathering tools in a form that never breaks! It contains logging, mining, and harvesting tools that can gather from any of their respective nodes. The tools will replace your existing tools on any character.
This part is interesting. "Finally. After months, I've perfected my ritual. I've written it in blood, just as the necromancers would."
This path leads back outside. We should go the other direction.
This personal journal relates one adventurer's foray into the Underworld. It describes some of the creatures found there.
This piece of parchment contains calculations that appear to be done by Scarlet's hand. She was trying to track how much weight her steam creatures could carry.
This piece of the Great Northern Wall has eroded. After 250 years of rain, wind, and snow, its edges are smoothed. It once kept Ascalon's enemies at bay. Now, it's returning to the land.
This place has gone dark, but there's enough Exalted magic lingering that we should be able to get this fellow up and running. We just need to extract the residue in a usable form.
This place has seen better days, but nothing a little elbow grease won't fix.
This place is much more...frenetic than my previous expeditions. The potential is high, but so are the stakes.
This place should work. Keep me safe, now. I can't be distracted.
This place will never be the same. What are we supposed to do now?
This plot of soil is ready for planting, but you don't have a seed pouch equipped.
This ranch is the source of all the beef consumed in Smokestead. Impressive, right? We couldn't survive without cattle, and these cattle are some of the finest.

This region is littered with dwarven artifacts that could yield ancient secrets of dealing with dragons. It is also home to hostile grawl, krait and ettins. Worse, the Risen have begun to move in from the south. The Durmand Priory and Vigil have forged an alliance to face these threats together in the forts of Concordia and Caer Evermore. Goldenlight Hallow Lab is devising new weapons to aid our cause.
This relatively new volume has a golden imprint on the cover that says "Winner of the Krytan Noble Prize 1324". The title of the book reads, "Wikki's Official Guide to Tyria."
This reservoir holds most of Shaemoor's drinking water. It's no surprise it's such a ripe target for bandits.
This sage did not come alone!
This saw blade could be fashioned into a makeshift bow, with some string.
This scrap pile contains both dredge and Flame Legion machinery.
This scroll case contains Eir's notes on sculpture.
This seems to be a miniature prototype for the probes scattered across the countryside. This one is off, but the others are much larger and have an unsettling red glow.
This sheet of parchment is fairly undamaged. The paper and the handwriting are familiar to you.
This shelf is dedicated to Snargle Goldclaw's novels, notes, and rough drafts. It is surprisingly well organized.
This short book details what is known about covert organizations through the ages, from the Shining Blade to the Order of Whispers.
This shrine bears an inscription.
This site's not bad at all, but it's going to need some defenses.
This situation is scary, but you have the strength to resist.

This sketch—probably drawn by Scarlet—is of some stone circles with rays of magic shooting through them. The notations imply her suspicion that this occurs naturally in certain places throughout Tyria.
This sliver hit the side of Rata Sum.
This snowman could use some finishing touches.
This spot should do.
This spot works for me.
This statue seems different. Sacred, somehow...or maybe just a little shinier. As you approach, you can't shake the feeling that you are being watched.
This story's too sad for me.
This strange item is new and without a layer of dust. The Inquest must have brought it in and left it behind.
This sunbeam looks brighter than it should be. A thick fog swirls within the beam.
This tablet has an engraving that reads: "The Final Speech of the Last Forgotten to the Exalted," transcribed by Bogani the Walker of Vabbi.
This team has one goal: cripple the centaurs. Wolf made it clear that I couldn't do it alone, so I hunt with this pack. And our prey doesn't stand a chance against us.
This text claims to be an interpretation of an ancient jotun writing. A poetic description of powerful forces that can move the very stars with their might.
This theoretical treatise discusses the control of magical energy as it applies to ghosts. Scholar Abel of the Durmand Priory theorizes that ghosts are just magical energy constructs.
This time, the grawl are worshipping something dangerous, something making them angry. Several hunters have vanished in those caves. I'm not letting another one go missing.
This tonic will turn you into a Nuhoch. The beetles will trust you, and you can herd them into the pen.
This tranformation cannot swim.
This trunk's lid is partially open. The interior holds old moth-eaten rags that might once have been clothing. There's nothing related to Turai Ossa.
This tunnel is just big enough for a skritt to go through. A boulder of the right size can block it off.
This unit is approaching equalization. At 20 stacks, equalization is imminent.
This unusual book has a lock mechanism with a coin slot. A message on the cover reads, "5 silver to open!"
This vase was likely once a statement of taste and wealth, but now it's crusted with the dirt and grime of passing centuries.
This volume chronicles the history of Cantha, and although the title and one passage make reference to the rite of Ascension, it does not cover the trials of the Forgotten or the divine fire.
This volume is a primer on the currently understood principles of magic. It does not cover the recent discoveries concerning ley lines, however.
This volume, written by a quaggan named Vloosaloo, describes a recipe for a love potion made from dried seaweed native to the Unending Ocean.
This wall sconce has survived the centuries, mostly intact. It still holds the torch that some previous intrepid explorer placed in it.
This was once Rata Sum's primary golem factory. My krewe is scouring the site for useful artifacts, as are the Inquest. You're not a spy, are you? Hmm. Your appearance doesn't suggest it.
This weapon did not belong to Artis Underfist. You have angered his spirit.
This weapon doesn't seem to suit this statue.
This weathered plaque appears to describe the crystal in front of you.
This will also disable automatic Travel Toy reuse.
This will be no problem.
This will help crack their codes, and hopefully save some lives.
This will silence you!
This will take them out.
This will teach me to listen to Faren. I hope we make it out of here so I can apply that lesson.
This won't work. Three strong voices of leadership, but they can't agree on anything!
This word is difficult to decipher. "Bounce"?
This—unit—is—not—a—garbage—receptacle.
Tholin was just saying the same thing about the moot diverting his people.
Thon polymorphe
Thorax d'Imuthi
Those Flame Legion rodents. They're more nuisance than dangerous...always trying to kill queens or loot nests to get at the eggs.
Those altered by Kralkatorrik are named "Branded" after this landmark. Survivors of the Branding say the conversion occurred instantly, those affected turning powerful and violent.
Those are all the settlements I'm aware of in the Riverlands. That's about all I can offer you.
Those are good words to live by, but there's a lot of bad blood here. Some of the old folks had family killed in the war.
Those are the ramblings of a crazy murderer. Make no mistake, honey. She enjoys killing. She needs to be found and put down.
Those are your only two choices?
Those bad leaf men, they took my friends into the cavern! They have cages there and make everyone feel very bad things. Please, can you free them?
Those centaur fleabags took our post at the Crossing. Never fear, though! We'll get it back!
Those choya were right on top of us. I get so used to seeing them around, I forget how dangerous they can be.
Those extractors can collect and use the wurm's own phytotoxins against it.
Those ghosts don't know what's coming. I'm here to take them out!
Those ghosts will soon be a thing of the past. You have been a great help!
Those guys better not die on me.
Those money-grubbing connivers? It's bad enough I lost my boyfriend to those shady "businessmen." Take my advice: reject their advances. Nothing good will come of their machinations.
Those rats are running from something.
Those shinies look so lovely. Climb up and carry them down!
Those skritt are going to tear up the lab! We need to get them out of there, now!
Those slimy vermin will think twice before stealing supplies from my haven!
Those spider eggs are killing our hounds! The spiders will wipe out the whole kennel at this rate. We need to get rid of those eggs, as well as the spiders laying them!
Those vile Forged! Joko preserve us!
Those who lost the gift ran on, then stumbled, then fell. We could not look back.
Those wurms have scuttled my experiments for the last time. Time to power up the golem and start squishing!
Those wyverns will attack anything they see. Including us!
Though I know I need to, it's hard to let go.

Though dusty and clearly abandoned, this book is in remarkable condition. The title reads, "The Vizier of the Tower: Benevolence or Madness?" Scrawled inside the cover is, "Property of Mollen, Esteemed Explorer."
Though it is true that she's always trying to bear the weight of the whole world.
Though the Vanguard were used to the horrors of charr battles, the civilians traveling with them were not. Many broke off from the caravan, fleeing in terror as the monsters set upon us.
Though the worthy pursue me, I can only be sought. The best don't stop trying, but I cannot be caught. What am I?
Threat identified.
Three cheers for Ascalon!
